latest.question: Deputy Michael Cahill asked the Minister for Justice, Home Affairs and Migration to provide a year-by-year breakdown of the number of serving Garda members assigned to County Kerry from 1996 to 2026, including a breakdown by Garda district and individual Garda station, in tabular form.
latest.reply:
I propose to take Questions Nos. 603, 609 and 611 together.
The Garda Commissioner is responsible for the management and administration of An Garda Síochána under Section 33 of the Policing, Security and Community Safety Act 2024, which includes the distribution and stationing of Garda personnel throughout the State. The Commissioner is independent in his functions under Section 34 of the Act.
I am assured that Garda management keeps the distribution of resources under ongoing review. When allocating and transferring Gardaí to and from any Division or Unit, An Garda Síochána must take account of the annual policing plan and consider a range of factors, including local and national crime trends and workloads; policing arrangements and operational strategies; local population and trends as well as the geographical area.
An Garda Síochána publishes information in relation to the allocation of Gardaí nationally, including a breakdown of Garda divisions and stations nationwide. Data on the number of Gardaí allocated to the Kerry Division, from 2006 - 2025, along with the same data for 2026 can be found here:
www.garda.ie/en/information-centre/garda-statistics/human%20resources/
I am advised by the Garda authorities that the table below provides the number of Gardaí assigned to dedicated community policing teams in Tralee and Killarney respectively in each of the past 5 years.
It should be noted that An Garda Síochána police on a Divisional basis using all resources in a Community

latest.question: Deputy Michael Cahill asked the Minister for Justice, Home Affairs and Migration if An Garda Síochána maintains statistics on response times to serious incidents requiring an urgent Garda response in County Kerry; and if so, to provide the average response times for each of the past five years, broken down by Garda district or station where available.
latest.reply:
I propose to take Questions Nos. 604, 606 and 607 together.
An Garda Síochána have advised that the CSO publishes reported crime statistics at Divisional level, including Kerry, for crime types including Discharging a Firearm, Possession of a Firearm, Weapons and Explosives Offences, Chemical Weapons Offences, Attempts/Threats to Murder, Assaults, Harassment and Related Offences, Assault Causing Harm, Criminal Damage and Arson from the Q1 2003 to the Q2 2026 period here:
data.cso.ie/table/CJQ10
Garda authorities also advise that there is no structured field available in PULSE to allow An Garda Síochána to definitively report that a crime incident is or was related to a feud.
In areas affected by feuding-related incidents, An Garda Síochána has initiated targeted operations and investigations led by Senior Investigative Officers. Enforcement measures include the deployment of armed support units, high-visibility patrols, checkpoints, and coordinated days of action. When individuals are charged with related offences, Gardaí routinely object to bail or seek the imposition of strict court bail conditions. Beyond law enforcement, the Kerry Local Community Safety Partnership provides an avenue for collaborative, multi-agency approaches to address these issues.
As is the case across the country, An Gardaí Síochána provide a 24/7 service and respond to calls for service and all emergencies through calls received and logged in regional control centres. Each call is assessed and priori

latest.question: Deputy Michael Cahill asked the Minister for Justice, Home Affairs and Migration the funding schemes and supports currently available to assist local authorities and communities in County Kerry with the installation and expansion of CCTV systems in towns and villages.
latest.reply:
CCTV in public places can play an important role in supporting community safety and providing reassurance to the public. While the use of CCTV by An Garda Síochána and local authorities can bring significant benefits, its operation must be carefully managed to ensure that it is lawful, necessary and proportionate and complies with data protection requirements.
Part 5 of the Garda Síochána (Recording Devices) Act 2023 was commenced on 14 October 2026. The commencement of Part 5, together with related transitional arrangements and the publication of the Garda CCTV Code of Practice, establishes a new statutory framework for the authorisation and operation of public CCTV schemes, repealing section 38 of the Garda Síochána Act 2005. The Code of Practice and supporting guidance are publicly available.
Under the new framework, only local authorities or An Garda Síochána may be authorised to operate public CCTV schemes. Existing CCTV schemes authorised under section 38 of the 2005 Act may continue to operate for a period of up to four years from commencement, or until their authorisation is revoked by the Garda Commissioner, whichever occurs first. Applications submitted before 2 April 2025 on which a decision remains pending will continue to be processed under the previous legislative framework.

latest.question: Deputy Cian O'Callaghan asked the Minister for Justice, Home Affairs and Migration the reason there is no phone number available for the Ukraine Crisis Temporary Accommodation Team; and the reason there are no social workers assigned to support and manage vulnerable Ukrainian families, like there is for families in IPAS accommodation.
latest.reply:
Persons availing of Temporary Protection can raise any concerns that they may have through a dedicated helpdesk, available at ukrainetempaccom@justice.ie .
The international and domestic legislation, frameworks and obligations for those seeking international protection (IPs) and beneficiaries of Temporary Protection differ significantly. In essence, those in receipt of Temporary Protection can access State services (with a small number of restrictions) in line with those granted to citizens of any EU Member State. As the Deputy will be aware, this is not the case for IPs.
There is no obligation on the State to provide social workers for people availing of Temporary Protection. Where a vulnerability arises, those in receipt of Temporary Protection can access relevant support services on the same basis as any Irish citizen.

latest.question: Deputy Roderic O'Gorman asked the Minister for Social Protection for an update on the achievement of commitment 5 - private sector, of the National Human Rights Strategy for Disabled People 2025-2030.
latest.reply:
The National Human Rights Strategy for Disabled People 2025-2030 is Ireland’s plan to advance the realisation of the UN Convention on the Rights of People with Disabilities. The strategy adopts a whole-of-Government approach across five pillars. My colleague, the Minister for Enterprise, Tourism and Employment, and I are jointly leading the employment pillar. The first action plan under the strategy covers the period 2025-2026.
With regard to Action 5.1, we are in the final stages of developing this media campaign to promote the employment of disabled people. The initial focus will be on employers. It will launch later this month through television, radio, print and social media channels. In the meantime, we are running Wage Subsidy Scheme and Work and Access ads on my Department's social media channels.
In regard to Action 5.2, Budget 2027 provided for an increase in the hours for ongoing Communication Support/Irish Sign Language interpreting from 24 to 48 hours and induction support from 12 to 18 hours under Work and Access. The guidelines and application forms were updated and simplified in April 2026. WorkAbility and Employability continue to support disabled customers into employment.

latest.reply:

latest.question: Deputy Cian O'Callaghan asked the Minister for Social Protection if he will examine the interaction between employment-status classifications, PAYE reporting, Special Collection PRSI arrangements and eligibility for MyFutureFund; whether procedures exist to review cases where a worker pays class A PRSI but does not appear in PAYE reporting data; and whether a revised employment-status determination can result in the correction of PAYE records for automatic-enrolment purposes.
latest.reply:
The introduction of a pensions auto-enrolment system was a Programme for Government commitment, and one of my key priorities. The aim of introducing an AE system is to address the pension coverage gap that exists in Ireland, and to help provide for better retirement incomes for employees.
The new system, which is called MyFutureFund, commenced on the 1st January 2026 and it is overseen by the National Automatic Enrolment Retirement Savings Authority (NAERSA), which is a separate statutory body, independent of my Department and directly responsible for all operational elements of MyFutureFund.
Under the provisions of the Automatic Enrolment Savings System Act 2024, prospective participants will be automatically enrolled in MyFuture if they are an employee and:
• They are aged between 23 and 60.
• They earn more than €20,000 per year across all employments, or more than €5,000 over a 13-week period.
• They are not currently actively paying into a pension through payroll, and the pension complies with the minimum contribution standards set out in regulations under the Act.
It is not possible to seek a formal determination or review of eligibility from NAERSA where the underlying PAYE classification is disputed as the NAERSA has no power to determine employment status or to instruct that corrections are to be made to PAYE records. latest.question: Deputy Paul Nicholas Gogarty asked the Minister for Social Protection the measures that can be introduced to ensure that women who lose their employment through no fault of their own during pregnancy are not left without adequate financial support when their baby arrives.
latest.reply:
I propose to take Questions Nos. 576, 579, 588, 589 and 598 together.
The Maternity Protection Acts 1994–2004 provide legal protection for those who are pregnant including in matters of employment and unfair dismissal. The Minister for Children, Disability and Equality has legal and policy responsibility in this area. My Department has responsibility for the payment of the associated Maternity Benefit income support.
Under the Maternity Protection Act, 1994, a claimant must be in employment immediately before the first day of her maternity leave.
Maternity Benefit is a statutory payment made for 26 weeks to employed and self-employed women who are on maternity leave from work and who have a certain number of paid PRSI contributions on their social insurance record.
While a woman who is made redundant before maternity leave begins cannot take maternity leave from the former employer because the employment has ended, she may still qualify for Maternity Benefit subject to meeting the statutory PRSI conditions. This approach is broadly consistent with other EU countries that entitlement to maternity income support is linked to social insurance rather than continued employment at the commencement of maternity leave.

examples.question: Deputy Paul Donnelly asked the Minister for Defence if she is aware of Irish Defence Forces members participating in military competitions with the Israeli Defence Forces; and if confirmed, her views on such on participation.
examples.reply:
The Defence Forces participate in international military competitions in order to promote in the Defence Forces the adoption of international best practice, exchange of tactics, techniques and procedures (TTP) and encourage the development of military skills. It also contributes to the development of particular military skillsets and doctrines.
The decision on who to invite to these competitions lies with the hosting nation. I am informed by the military authorities that the Defence Forces have not participated in any military competitions organised by the Israeli Defence Forces. I am also informed that, to date, no Defence Forces team has reported Israeli Defence Forces participation in competitions attended by Defence Forces personnel.

examples.question: Deputy Erin McGreehan asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine for an update on the timeline and commencement dates for the basic income support for sustainability scheme.
examples.reply:
My Department is fully committed to making payments to farmers under the various schemes at the earliest date possible and to the maximum number of farmers possible. This commitment to farmers is evidenced in the very high payment rates achieved across all schemes over the last number of years in both EU and Exchequer funded schemes.
The timelines for all schemes, including the planned payment dates, have been set after extensive consultation with farmers and taking account of application systems, monitoring systems, validation and processing systems and payment systems.
In 2025, my Department commenced payments under the Basic Income Support for Sustainability (BISS) scheme from October 16th ensuring money flowed as soon as practically possible to farmers.
This payment date is in line with the traditional payment date of the BISS Scheme to farmers and is as outlined in the Farmers' Charter.

examples.question: Deputy Tom Brabazon asked the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage for an update on the financial contribution scheme; and the rationale to no longer fund this scheme.
examples.reply:
The Government’s new housing plan, Delivering Homes, Building Communities 2025-2030, includes measures to increase delivery of housing for older people through increased delivery of social housing, increased delivery of more suitable homes in private housing and increased choice to support voluntary rightsizing, including a review of the operation of existing local authority financial contribution schemes.
I understand that existing financial contribution schemes in place in some local authorities are non-statutory and therefore a matter for the individual local authorities. Consideration will be given to a review of the operation of existing local authority financial contribution schemes and my Department is advancing these measures now incorporated in the new housing plan.

examples.question: Deputy Réada Cronin asked the Minister for Climate, Energy and the Environment what specific regulatory changes are being sought by Re-Turn for the proposed rPET reprocessing facility; the Department's position on the establishment of such a processing facility.
examples.reply:
Re-turn is a producer-led and owned, not-for-profit company established by beverage producers to meet their obligations under the Separate Collection (Deposit Return Scheme) Regulations.
Re-turn has stated its ambition to develop an rPET reprocessing facility in Ireland. In this regard, Re-turn has briefed me and Departmental officials on its plans.
The matter remains under consideration, with the Department considering the various public policy considerations that arise.

examples.question: Deputy John Paul O'Shea asked the Minister for Transport further to Parliamentary Question No.199 of 16 April 2026, regarding Ireland's current position (details supplied); whether he has articulated this position either internally with Irish officials or with European counterparts; if so, if he will provide details of what was articulated and through which medium.
examples.reply:
I am aware of the concerns raised by car rental fleet operators regarding the Clean Corporate Vehicles proposal. We engage regularly with representatives from this sector and have met with them several times over the past year, including discussions specifically on this proposal.
It should be noted that the measure remains at proposal stage, with negotiations currently underway at EU level. The Regulation will not be finalised until such time as an agreement is reached between the Council and the European Parliament. This process is expected to run through 2026, which intersects with Ireland’s Presidency of the Council of the EU.

examples.question: Deputy Paul Murphy asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine the numerical, scientific and editorial verification carried out before the Wildlife Unit End of Year Report for 2025 that was approved for publication; whether further errors have since been identified; and whether his Department will publish an amended report clearly identifying all corrections.
examples.reply:
The Wildlife Report compiled by my Department has stated that there was 7,625 badger captures in the vaccine area in 2025. This is the correct figure. The figure of 8,123 is the number of badger captures that were recorded in vaccine areas for 2024. Table 4 in the report states the correct figures of badger captures for 2024 and 2025.
For the purposes of clarity the figure for 2024 will be removed from the body of the text.

examples.question: Deputy Carol Nolan asked the Minister for Social Protection the number of people who have had their receipt of jobseeker's allowance or jobseeker's benefit permanently withdrawn or revoked for breach of the conditions associated with their claim, and who have not subsequently had their claim reinstated, from January 2020 to date.
examples.reply:
To be eligible for a Jobseeker's payment a person must satisfy all the eligibility criteria for the relevant scheme.
Where a claim has been stopped, it will only be re-instated following an application by the customer and where all conditions of the scheme are satisfied.
It is not possible to provide data on the number of claims stopped and not subsequently re-instated due to the large churn on jobseekers schemes and the many legitimate reasons that claims are stopped.
I trust that this clarifies matters for the Deputy.

examples.question: Deputy Ruth Coppinger asked the Minister for Social Protection the annual figures since 2015 for appeals lodged with the social welfare appeals office querying a refusal based on the habitual residence condition, by Irish citizens and non-Irish nationals, in tabular form.
examples.reply:
I am advised by the Chief Appeals Officer that the Social Welfare Appeals Office does not collate data on appeals specifically relating to the Habitual Residence Condition, therefore the statistical information is not available.
I trust this clarifies the matter for the Deputy.

examples.question: Deputy John Paul O'Shea asked the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage the number of appeals involving the rating of agricultural or horticultural buildings have been brought before the Valuation Tribunal since 2020; the number that were successful; and the average length of time taken to determine these appeals.
examples.reply:
As the Valuation Tribunal is independent in the performance of its functions, my Department does not hold the information requested in relation to the number of appeals involving the rating of agricultural or horticultural buildings have been brought before the Valuation Tribunal since 2020; the number that were successful; or the average length of time taken to determine these appeals.
It is noted that certain information on Valuation Tribunal appeals activity is included in the Tribunal's Annual Reports, available on the organisation's website at: www.valuationtribunal.ie/about-us/publications/.
Judgements of the Valuation Tribunal are also published and can be accessed on the Tribunal's website (at: www.valuationtribunal.ie/judgments/) under 'Name', 'Year', 'Property category' and 'Rating Authority'. It is noted that the Tribunal does not, however, include a specific category of appeal termed 'agriculture / horticultural'.
The Deputy may wish to contact the Tribunal directly in relation to the information sought by emailing info@valuationtribunal.ie.

examples.question: Deputy Paul Lawless asked the Minister for Transport for a record of all reported accidents, collisions, or safety incidents that have occurred at or in the vicinity of the unmarked traffic islands in Ballindine, County Mayo, on the N17, over the past 20 years; if road safety audits or assessments have been carried out at this location; and if there are plans to install appropriate road markings or safety measures at this site.
examples.reply:
As Minister for Transport, I have responsibility for overall policy and exchequer funding in relation to the National Roads Programme. Under the Roads Acts 1993-2015 and in line with the National Development Plan (NDP), the operation and management of individual national roads is a matter for Transport Infrastructure Ireland (TII), in conjunction with the local authorities concerned. This is also subject to the Infrastructure Guidelines and the necessary statutory approvals. In this context, TII is best placed to advise you in relation to safety on the N17 at Ballindine, Co. Mayo.
The Government is committed to reducing road deaths and creating safer roads for everyone in Ireland.
Noting the above position, I have referred your question to TII for a direct reply. Please advise my private office if you do not receive a reply within 10 working days.
